## Reserve a face or fill a solid mask (`custom; solid`) {#sec-ch11-custom}

### Summary

Both callbacks exist for a caller that writes the ghosts itself. A `custom` face keeps a non-null entry in
the callback table, so every physical-face predicate of @sec-ch11-registry is true there while the
callback writes nothing; the user code or layout that installed it owns the fill. The corner refresh after an
exchange is the one exception: on a cubed-sphere block it treats an $x_2$ or $x_3$ face that holds the built-in
`custom` no-op as owned by the panel exchange (@sec-ch03-cornerrefresh). A `solid` face is the
mask-fill primitive: on a Boolean mask, one means solid, and the rectification of @sec-ch11-solids uses the
callback to declare every ghost slab solid before it sweeps.
Neither callback introduces a PDE[^rg-8c4d78431fa1] discretization.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Reserve a callback or fill a mask with ones.

**Data.** Supplied tensor; Boolean one denotes solid only on a mask.

**Placement.** Physical fill; solid callbacks also prepare mask rectification.

**Activation.** `custom` and `solid` are explicit face names; default off.

**Guarantee / limits.** Custom is identity; solid is constant fill, not a hydro wall.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test limits are in the Tests layer; solver ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

### Derivation

No PDE discretization is introduced. The custom map is the identity on the supplied tensor. The solid map
replaces every entry of the ghost slab by one. Reapplying either map returns the same tensor, so both are
idempotent and satisfy the registry contract. For a Boolean mask, one denotes solid; for a hydro state vector
it is merely the number one in every row and is not a physical state construction.
`custom_inner` and `custom_outer`
([`bc_func.cpp:7-8`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L7-L8))
have empty bodies; `solid_inner` and `solid_outer`
([`bc_func.cpp:68-87`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L68-L87))
assign one to the width-$n_g$ slab. Check C1 verifies the identity and the constant-one ghost fill without
assuming a thermodynamic meaning [check `src/snapy_report/ch11/checks/boundary_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch11/checks/boundary_check.out`]. The checks do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

Custom keeps a non-null callback slot for a user or layout operation and is called like any other callback
by the physical fills and the corner refresh of @sec-ch11-timing. On an $x_2$ or $x_3$ face of a cubed-sphere block
the built-in no-op also marks the face as exchange-owned for that refresh, which then re-applies the $x_1$ functions
inside the face's ghost slab. `is_custom_noop` recognises the no-op by function identity, so a function a caller
installs on the face keeps it physical even when the face's name is still `custom`
({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp is_custom_noop >}}; @sec-ch03-cornerrefresh). Solid acts on all rows of the tensor it is
given and skips a collapsed direction. `InternalBoundaryImpl::rectify_solid`
({{< code src/bc/rectify_solid.cpp InternalBoundaryImpl::rectify_solid >}}) applies the solid callbacks to
its mask on every direction with more than one cell before the directional sweeps, and after the sweeps
applies the callbacks its caller supplies. No independent spatial accuracy order applies.

@fig-ch11-custom-stencil illustrates the operations, with labelled roles independent of colour.

```{python}

#| fig-cap: "Reserve a face or fill a solid mask. Schematic only; no simulation measurements."
#| fig-alt: "Labelled schematic of the custom boundary operation; ghosts and owned cells have separate text labels."
#| echo: false
```

### Code

**How to use.** Install the user ghost fill before reconstruction consumes it. The YAML name reserves a physical
face but does not install a user algorithm. Use the `solid` callback on the rectification mask, not as a physical
hydro state.

This is a configuration fragment, not a standalone simulation deck.

```yaml
boundary-condition:
  external:
    x1-inner: custom
    x1-outer: custom
```

The generated recipe below installs and tests a Python zero-gradient fill.

**Refusals and prerequisites.** Neither callback checks whether the supplied tensor has a physical interpretation.
Custom silently preserves stale ghosts if the caller fails to fill them; parser name/key refusals remain those of
@sec-ch11-registry.

**Read the implementation.** `solid_inner` ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp BC_FUNCTION overload=9 >}}) contains:

```cpp
var.narrow(dim, 0, nghost) = 1;
```

The assignment is the constant map in the Derivation layer. On a Boolean mask it declares the whole ghost slab solid; the empty custom body is the identity map.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |

| solidbc | [`bc_func.cpp:68-87`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L68-L87) | `solid_inner` | `solid` |
| rectify | {{< code src/bc/rectify_solid.cpp InternalBoundaryImpl::rectify_solid >}} | `rectify_solid` | `boundary-condition/internal/max-iter` |
| classify | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_wall_boundary >}} | `is_wall_boundary` | none |
| no-op by identity | {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp is_custom_noop >}} | `is_custom_noop` | `custom` on $x_2$/$x_3$, cubed sphere |

: Implementation sites for custom. {#tbl-ch11-custom-code}

1. Leave the tensor unchanged for custom. The anchor `custom_inner` is in
   [`bc_func.cpp:7-8`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L7-L8).
2. For solid, assign one to the requested ghost slab. The anchor `solid_inner` is in
   [`bc_func.cpp:68-87`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L68-L87).
3. Use solid on a mask; do not infer a hydro wall from the function name. The anchor `rectify_solid` is in
   {{< code src/bc/rectify_solid.cpp InternalBoundaryImpl::rectify_solid >}}.

### Tests

The minimal callback runtime check is recorded as `ch11-custom` in
`tools/do-cards.yaml`; its `run.check` verifies CPU dtype, aliasing, interior
preservation and repeated slab fills through the N8 runner.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_rectify.release` | After rectification of an $8^3$ mask with two solid cells, every inner and outer ghost slab is solid | exact equality to one | test fixture (`nghost`[^rg-fd6fa2a1ed93] 1 without a block) |
| `boundary_check.py` (report only) | `[C1]` as described below | exact | symbolic, rational or integer identity |

: Source-test assertions and report-only checks for custom. {#tbl-ch11-custom-tests}

The assertion is the ghost-slab loop of `test2` ({{< code tests/test_rectify.cpp test2 >}}).

**Not provided:** a round-off derivation for each tolerance, because the cited tests give acceptance
criteria without deriving each round-off bound, and this book does not derive those bounds.
Device/rank distinctions and missing runs are recorded in @sec-ch15-ch11.

The report-only checks `[C1]` establish that copy, parity, idempotence and corner ownership hold
exactly.[^ch11-custom-run]
These checks exercise report formulas, not the compiled boundary kernels. The source-test table records
assertions and tolerances, not new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver results.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A custom no-op does not supply missing physical ghost data, and a non-null custom face still passes
`is_physical_boundary`; only the corner refresh on a cubed-sphere block treats the built-in no-op on $x_2$ or $x_3$
as exchange-owned (@sec-ch03-cornerrefresh). Using solid on a hydro tensor writes literal ones; it does not construct a no-slip
or thermodynamic wall. The callbacks a caller passes to the rectification must be callable: the loop does not
guard null entries.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. The callback recipe
checks CPU fills only; it does not validate solid-wall kernels, CUDA or multi-rank behavior.
:::
